children: Services led sectors with 47 per cent share, while programmatic accounted for 96 per cent of digital ad impressions

India’s digital advertising market continued to maintain strong momentum in the first seven months of 2026, with digital ad impressions rising 44 per cent in January-July 2026 compared with the corresponding period last year, according to the latest TAM AdEx report.

The services sector retained its position as the largest contributor, accounting for 47 per cent of digital ad impressions during the period. Personal Healthcare and Textiles/Clothing entered the top 10 sectors during January-July 2026.

At the category level, Ecom-Other Services emerged as the leading category, accounting for 10 per cent of digital ad impressions. It replaced Ecom-Online Shopping, which was the top category during January-July 2025.
Ecom-Real Estate was the other new entrant to the top 10 categories. Collectively, the top 10 categories accounted for 45 per cent of digital ad impressions during the period.

Among the top 10 fastest-growing categories, Ecom-Other Services recorded an 85 per cent increase in ad impressions over January-July 2025. Lifestyle recorded the highest growth at 92 per cent, followed by Ecom-Real Estate at 90 per cent, Ecom-Travel & Tourism at 71 per cent, Software at 51 per cent and Multiple Courses at 49 per cent.
Overall, ad impressions increased across more than 280 categories during the period.
Adobe Software India emerged as the largest advertiser on digital during January-July 2026, accounting for 4 per cent of ad impressions. Flipkart.com and OpenAI followed with 3 per cent each.
Amazon Online India and Reliance Retail accounted for 2 per cent each, while Hindustan Unilever, Google, Info Edge India, Myntra Designs and Facebook Inc each recorded a 1 per cent share.

The report also identified more than 1.1 lakh exclusive digital advertisers during January-July 2026. Attitudist, in the ecom-clothing/textile/fashion category, emerged as the leading digital-only advertiser compared with television.

Instagram remained the leading web publisher during January-July 2026, accounting for 69 per cent of digital ad impressions. It was followed by Facebook.com at 41 per cent, YouTube.com at 23 per cent and X.com at 15 per cent among the next 10 web publishers.
The top five web publishers collectively accounted for 83 per cent of digital ad impressions during the period.
Display continued to dominate digital advertising, accounting for 91 per cent of ad impressions, while video contributed the remaining 9 per cent.

Programmatic remained the dominant transaction method, accounting for 96 per cent of digital ad impressions. Ad Networks accounted for 2 per cent, with the remaining share coming from direct, programmatic/ad network and other transaction methods.
